title: How accurate is the crowd count?

headline.dataset: VisDrone2020-CC (DroneCrowd), 82 annotated sequences, 3 frames each, 1920x1080 drone video
headline.plain_english: On average the detector finds about 89% of the people really in the frame (median), with a typical error of 51 people (32%). It orders scenes by crowd size well (rank correlation 0.83).

validation_runs.name: Juelich entrance experiment, 75 people, 65 s
validation_runs.detector: orange-cap colour detector (special-purpose, not a general detector)
validation_runs.note: Overhead fixed camera, indoor controlled experiment with volunteers. The detector over-counts by about 5, probably people past the gate whose tracks have ended (not verified).

validation_runs.name: DroneCrowd sequence 023, about 260 people, 12 s
validation_runs.note: The true crowd barely changes, so correlation is not meaningful; the detector finds a steady 71% of it.

charts.title: Concert clip: risk over time
charts.caption: Risk climbs from LOW to HIGH as the drone's view takes in more of the crowd. This is the camera revealing people, not a crowd arriving.

charts.title: DroneCrowd 023: detected vs true people
charts.caption: Detected people against ground truth over 12 seconds.

charts.title: Juelich entrance experiment: risk and counts
charts.caption: A crush at a 0.5 m gate clearing over 65 s, with the surge and sustained-high alerts marked.

limits: Detection undercounts packed crowds, and tightly packed seated rows seen from above are missed most.
The risk score is relative to how many people are found. D_CRIT is tuned per clip, so LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH are illustrative, not validated against real danger.
No dataset contains a real stampede, so the demo shows density and alerts, not a stampede.
The Juelich result uses a colour-based detector that only works for orange caps, on overhead camera footage, not a drone.
Alert thresholds (3 s hold, 8 risk points per second) are defaults that have not been tuned on varied footage.
